thread:
maya: quick heads up — onboarding gate failed for clairvoyant-7b, CI flagged a schema compatibility issue in config.json. i started a quick run but wanted to ping folks who own tokenizer/weights parity.
config-lint-bot: FAILURE: schema validation error - path `tokenizer.special_tokens` missing (expected object) ; allowed: null | object. See /tmp/lint/clairvoyant-7b/config.json: line 42
ops-bot: deploy-checker: model-ingest job #4521 failed (exit code 1). logs: https://ci.redwood/run/4521/logs
jia: can you paste the offending snippet? i can try a minimal patch if it's just a missing field.
maya: sure — here's the relevant part from the manifest we got from the partner: ```json
"tokenizer": {
  "vocab_uri": "gs://models/clairvoyant-7b/vocab.json",
  "merges_uri": null
}
```

maya: note: their tokenizer expects default special tokens inside serving to be inferred; our schema requires explicit `special_tokens` object (we recently tightened this for deterministic padding).
sam: ugh, that tightened schema is biting again. options: 1) patch the manifest with a minimal `special_tokens` object, 2) relax the schema to allow null/omitted and apply runtime defaults, 3) special-case this model in the gate.
ryan: i'd prefer 1 for the short term — add the minimal object in the onboarding PR and get it through the gate, then open a follow-up to discuss schema relaxation. less blast radius.
jia: i'll open a quick PR to add the missing field and a test that validates defaulting behavior. pinging @sam for review since you're owner of tokenizer defaults. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/1426
sam: ack, i'll take a look in ~30m. quick question — do we also need to check weights uri? last time a symlink in GCS caused runtime to try to deref and fail.
maya: good call — ops-bot attached the ingest log earlier. snippet shows `weights_uri: gs://models/clairvoyant-7b/weights` and the job error was `IOError: object not found` when trying to open weights/manifest. could be a symlink folder layout mismatch.
ellie: i can run a quick `gsutil ls -L` on that path and confirm. if it's a directory with symlinked objects we should rewrite the weights pointer to the resolved object for the PR.
config-lint-bot: SUGGESTION: add schema comment `# auto-filled-by-onboard` to the new field to make future automation obvious.
jia: added the field in the branch and included a unit test that asserts `tokenizer.special_tokens` has default fields if missing. also updated the onboarding script to resolve weights URIs when they point to composite objects. link to branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/tree/hotfix/clairvoyant-7b-tokenizer-fix
ryan: thanks. can we gate the PR on the unit test + a manual `gsutil ls` confirmation?
jia: yes — pushing a commit with an automated `gsutil` check in the CI job; it will fail fast if weights path is non-resolvable.
maya: perfect. once sam approves we can merge and re-run the ingest job. if anything else shows up i'll post here. :thumbsup:
sam: reviewed, left two tiny nits (naming of the test and one log message). approving after fixes. :white_check_mark:
maya: merged PR #1426, re-triggering ingest job now: https://ci.redwood/run/4521/logs/triggered
ops-bot: deploy-checker: new run #4522 started — will report back.
config-lint-bot: NOTE: follow-up issue recommended: consider schema change to accept null tokenizer.special_tokens + explicit runtime defaulting (link to internal RFC: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/2026-tokenizer-defaults).
maya: filing follow-up ticket to eng-ml backlog per recommendation. thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.
ryan: nice — great async flow.
ellie: gsutil check was clean, weights path resolved to a single manifest object. all good on my end.
ops-bot: deploy-checker: run #4522 succeeded. ingest -> ready. :tada:
maya: closing the loop — model moved to serve-ready. will add a short postmortem item about schema ergonomics to the backlog.
